title: Be There for the Beginning: Celebrate the Launch of NVIDIA RTX Spark
body: Be There for the Beginning: Celebrate the Launch of NVIDIA RTX Spark Explore a new era of local AI, join launch celebrations around the world and #ShareYourSpark. October 15, 2026 by Shreevar Rastogi 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! A new beginning for Windows PCs starts tomorrow with the launch of NVIDIA RTX Spark — one PC built for creators, gamers and AI agents. All are invited to celebrate with NVIDIA and partners at launch events around the world. Share Your Spark Every PC has a story. What was your first Windows PC, and what did it spark a love for? Join the celebration online by sharing responses with #ShareYourSpark for a chance to win an ASUS ProArt P14 RTX Spark laptop signed by NVIDIA founder and CEO Jensen Huang. See the campaign and official rules . See What Reviewers Are Saying From local AI workflows to creative apps and gaming, see what reviewers are saying about RTX Spark — then experience it at a launch celebration. “The fact that NVIDIA, Microsoft and their partners have delivered such a capable, compatible and polished platform even in its first at-bat should put the rest of the PC industry on notice.” — Tom’s Hardware “I tested NVIDIA’s RTX Spark for gaming and local AI – the performance absolutely stunned me.” — TrustedReviews , UK “I’m very happy to report that performance is actually looking really good when it comes to AI, gaming and creative workflows.” — Microcenter “[RTX Spark] is a different species of computer that has arrived early. title: Open From Data Center to Desktop: NVIDIA Expands Nemotron Family With Highest Efficiency Super VL and Bolt Models
body: Open From Data Center to Desktop: NVIDIA Expands Nemotron Family With Highest Efficiency Super VL and Bolt Models 5x faster, accurate and customizable Nemotron 3.5 Super VL expands NVIDIA’s open models for always-on agents, with Nemotron 3.5 Bolt bringing agentic intelligence to local NVIDIA systems. October 15, 2026 by Kari Briski 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! NVIDIA today released Nemotron 3.5 Super VL, an open 120-billion-parameter model that delivers the fastest task completion and highest accuracy for specialized always-on agents. Joining it are two new edge models: Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B-A9B 24GB, optimized to balance intelligence and speed per GB for local agentic workloads, and Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B 4GB, optimized for intelligence per GB for fast conversational agents. Super VL and Bolt 74B-A9B are available now, with Bolt E4B coming Oct. 23. The three open models together cover the full range of agent deployments, from large enterprise servers down to edge devices and local hardware. Any organization that wants to run agents on NVIDIA infrastructure now has an open, optimized model for their tier, without having to choose between capability and deployability. Super VL and Bolt join the Nemotron family alongside Lightning and Ultra. Lightning, released in August, handles high-throughput workloads; Ultra handles the hardest reasoning tasks; and Bolt brings intelligence to the edge. Nemotron 3.5 Super VL: Frontier Accuracy at One-Fifth the Size Super VL, built in collaboration with the Nemotron Coalition , delivers leading accuracy on multimodal agentic tasks — instruction following, tool use, multistep business workflows, and visual understanding — comparable with NVIDIA’s largest reasoning model at roughly one-fifth the parameter count. Nemotron 3.5 Super VL delivers frontier-level intelligence in its class for high-volume agentic workflows. As the fastest open agentic model in its class — 5x faster than the next best — it helps enterprise agents complete high-volume tasks faster across workflows that span days or weeks. Nemotron 3.5 Super VL, on Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index leadboard, achieves up to 5x faster throughput compared to other models in its class. Unlike closed frontier models, organizations can post-train Super VL on their own data, deploy it on their own infrastructure and oversee what they build. Nemotron 3.5 Bolt: Agentic Intelligence at the Edge Bolt 74B-A9B 24GB is designed to run everyday agentic tasks locally on NVIDIA RTX/DGX Spark, using a native 2-bit quantization to fit in 24GB of memory and run alongside other applications. Relative to other models with a similar memory footprint, it provides a good balance of intelligence and speed: smart enough to get most jobs done, yet much faster than the smartest models. With Bolt 74B-A9B 24GB, users can delegate their projects to popular local agent harnesses — from researching the web to writing to debugging code — all without sending those workloads to the cloud. It is the #1 open model in its class on PinchBench , and the #2 open model for BrowseComp . Bolt E4B 4GB is built for physical and conversational agents on GeForce RTX, Jetson, and RTX/DGX Spark. It combines natural conversation with multi-turn agentic capabilities to power fast local voice assistants, interactive characters and embedded interfaces. Adoption of Custom Super Intelligence Dozens of organizations across industries are post-training Super VL on their own data, tools, policies and workflows to push accuracy higher on the specialized tasks that define their agent deployments. Super VL is being post-trained and customized by organizations across industries. Scale AI post-trained the model for Skydance’s vendor credit finance agent and for EY’s M&A due diligence agent. AfterQuery customized the model for Hebbia for credit agreement analysis. AI21 and Alice post-trained the model for cybersecurity attack resilience. Mercor post-trained the model on APEX-SWE coding benchmark, for coding agents that plan, write and debug code. ModelScope enables developers to fine-tune the model through its ms-swift framework for specialized multimodal applications. Additional organizations customizing Nemotron 3.5 Super VL include Ramp for financial document intelligence; Dream , sovereign AI-powered cybersecurity research and vulnerability analysis; Lila Sciences for scientific discovery and search, and R1 for medical claims analysis and revenue cycle management. TrainLoop post-trained the model with dermatology data from Nolla, which just became the first company approved for AI to write initial patient prescriptions. Software platform companies integrating Nemotron 3.5 Super VL include: Atlassian , for tasks like agentic search across apps such as Jira and Confluence. CrowdStrike , which is customizing the model for agentic blue teaming in enterprise security. Dassault Systèmes , powering engineering design and simulation. Perplexity , for search and agentic tasks in Perplexity Search and Computer. Salesforce , which is customizing Nemotron to power AI agents that digitize and automate complex government workflows in secure customer environments through Missionforce Operations. Synopsys software for semiconductor design verification interoperates with the model. What Nemotron 3.5 Super VL Actually Sees Nemotron 3.5 Super VL’s vision language strengths are targeted at what agents encounter in practice: optical character recognition, tables, charts and structured information in visual documents. It processes a web page, extracts text, reads graphs and charts, and returns insights from what it finds. The same applies to PDFs and other documents agents commonly work with. Nemotron 3.5 Super VL understands images, webpages and PDFs and acts on that understanding. Combining text and visual understanding in one model means agents don’t need to route tasks between separate systems — context carries through as work moves from document to data to decision. Open for Maximum Control, Security, and Privacy Openness and customizability reinforce each other. The model ships with open weights, open datasets and training recipes. Control runs in two directions. Organizations can run the model wherever their security and data-residency requirements dictate. They also choose to adopt a model they can adapt, rather than one subject to a provider’s restrictions. In insurance, for example, a customized agent can scan claims for fraud markers on repeat. In financial services, an agent can review credit scores and flag activity against an organization’s own lending criteria. The model stays on premises. The data stays private. Customization is supported through NVIDIA NeMo, Python-based pipelines and open datasets. Nemotron 3.5 Super VL was trained on about 26 trillion tokens across pretraining and continued pretraining, then post-trained with roughly 3.8 million samples and reinforcement learning across dozens of environments. NVIDIA is also releasing open datasets on Hugging Face spanning agentic tool use , finance, instruction following, long context, fairness and vision-language understanding, along with the reinforcement learning environments in NeMo Gym. NVIDIA NIM packages the model as a production-ready microservice with performance-optimized, validated configurations and enterprise-grade support, refreshed every two weeks with security patches and performance improvements. And with the model running on NVIDIA Dynamo, organizations can serve up to 8x more users with 85% lower latency. Nemotron 3.5 Super VL is available now on Hugging Face, Open Router, ModelScope community and as NVIDIA NIM. Runs on DGX Spark, DGX Station, and RTX Nemotron 3.5 Super VL runs across NVIDIA’s full hardware stack: on DGX Spark , DGX Station ,  RTX PRO and RTX systems for local intelligence at the desktop, on NVIDIA Jetson at the edge, and across data center and cloud environments. Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B-A9B 24G B is available now on Hugging Face, with support for llama.cpp, Ollama , LM Studio , Unsloth , and vLLM . Built for NVIDIA RTX Spark laptops arriving Oct. 16, it also runs on GeForce RTX PCs , DGX Spark , DGX Station and RTX PRO workstations . Download the open weights , explore customization resources with NVIDIA NeMo, or read the technical blog for the full architecture breakdown. Stay up to date on agents, NVIDIA Nemotron and more by subscribing to NVIDIA news , joining the community , and following NVIDIA AI on LinkedIn , Instagram , X and Facebook . title: Dial Up the Cloud: NVIDIA DLSS 4.5 Controls Arrive on GeForce NOW
body: Dial Up the Cloud: NVIDIA DLSS 4.5 Controls Arrive on GeForce NOW Plus, stream ‘Enshrouded’ 1.0 and ‘Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun 2’ alongside 10 new games this week. October 15, 2026 by GeForce NOW Community 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Dial in the next gaming session this GFN Thursday. New NVIDIA DLSS 4.5 controls give GeForce NOW members more choice over how supported games look and perform in the cloud, even without the latest hardware. Then, step into the Shroud as Keen Games’ Enshrouded leaves early access with its 1.0 release, or let the bolts fly in Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun 2 . Both are streaming on GeForce NOW at launch. With 10 new games joining the cloud this week, members can put the new controls to work in supported titles and keep playing across supported devices without downloads, installs or expensive hardware upgrades. Fine-Tune the Cloud With DLSS 4.5 Controls More control, more cloud power. NVIDIA DLSS 4.5 controls are now available on GeForce NOW, giving members more choice over how supported games look and perform in the cloud, even without the latest hardware. DLSS Super Resolution sharpens image quality, while Dynamic Multi Frame Generation delivers lower latency and reduces stutter for smoother streaming, and Ray Reconstruction enhances ray-traced visuals. In addition, Ultimate members streaming on GeForce RTX 5080-powered cloud rigs benefit from the maximum available options, including Dynamic Multi Frame Generation up to 4X. From James Bond’s globe-trotting missions in 007 First Light — now with path tracing support — to CONTROL Resonant ’s reality-bending Manhattan and the shadowy scares of Resident Evil Requiem , the controls help fine-tune supported games for image quality, responsiveness or a preferred balance between the two. These new settings are available in the GeForce NOW app under settings, for Windows, macOS, Chrome OS and Steam OS platforms. Members can read here for more details on using the feature with their membership tier, and more information on how to get the smoothest cloud game streaming for some games on GeForce NOW. Rise, Flameborn Enshrouded 1.0 brings the co-op survival action role-playing game out of early access and into its full release. Rise as a Flameborn, the last ember of hope of a dying race, and venture into a vast world of survival, action and role-playing, where a corrupting fog has consumed a once-beautiful kingdom. The title brings improvements to existing systems, alongside expansions in combat with nine new spells, new mage and archer skills, reworked wands and upgradeable Eternal spells and arrows. New enemy variants keep encounters fresh, while a new biome raises the player level cap to 50 and equipment cap to 55. GeForce NOW offers Enshrouded 1.0 ready to play in the cloud at launch across supported devices. Skip the 60GB local install to save precious storage space, then step into the Shroud without waiting for downloads or needing to make room for the update. Let the Bolts Fly Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun 2 is now streaming on GeForce NOW. The brutal, fast-paced sequel to the retro first-person shooter brings more enemies, more weapons and new ways to purge. Picking up directly after the original game, a branching single-player campaign sends the fight to grimdark new worlds. Choose between the formidable Sternguard Veteran Malum Caedo and the swift Sister of Battle Nyra Veyrath, each with distinct abilities, weapons and play styles. From towering hive cities to jungle mangrove swamps, new enemy types await in every biome. GeForce NOW keeps the campaign ready in the cloud. No local rig upgrades or game installs stand between members and the fight — the Emperor’s work waits for no loading bar. In addition, members can look for the following joining the GeForce NOW library : Deep Dish Dungeon (New release on Steam , Oct. 13) Planet Zoo 2 (New release on Steam , Oct. 13) Total War: SHOGUN 2 – Complete Edition (New release on Steam , Oct. 13) Valor Mortis (New release on Steam , Oct. 13) Among the Trolls (New release on Steam , Oct. 14) over the hill (New release on Steam , Oct. 14) Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun 2 (New release on Steam , Oct. 14) Beyond These Stars (New release on Steam and Xbox , Oct. 15), available on Game Pass Tenebris Somnia (New release on Steam , Oct. 16) The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt – Remastered ( Xbox ), available on Microsoft Store Also this week, the performance of DLSS 5’s 3D-Guided Neural Rendering model is improving by 2X, enabling even more gamers to enjoy DLSS 5’s transformative uplift in lighting and materials at high frame rates and settings. The new, more performant DLSS 5 model will debut in NBA 2K27 on Oct. 16 on GeForce NOW, GeForce RTX 50 Series GPUs and RTX Spark laptops. Dates listed above reflect when games are released on their respective stores. GeForce NOW availability may vary, as games are onboarded after they’re released and added throughout the week. Keep an eye on GeForce NOW channels and GFN Thursdays for availability updates to announced titles. Gamers who want to test out the new 4.5 controls and high-performance GeForce NOW cloud gaming can start with a day pass to try premium cloud gaming before committing to a membership. Better yet, the cost of the day pass can be applied toward a first monthly membership — making it easy to try GeForce RTX-powered cloud gaming with the latest releases, then level up for more. What’s on the playlist this weekend? Let us know on X or in the comments below. Categories: Gaming Tags: Cloud Gaming Gaming GeForce NOW Related News AI NVIDIA Expands Advanced Technology Access for Europe’s Scientific Community Through Open Learning Resources, Collaborations and Compute Oct 15, 2026 AI The Nordics and NVIDIA Show What’s Possible When a Region Commits to Advanced Computing Oct 14, 2026 AI NVIDIA Announces New Investments in the UK Startup Ecosystem Oct 13, 2026 AI All Systems Go: Global PC App Ecosystem Ready for NVIDIA RTX Spark Oct 13, 2026

title: Staffing Business Owner and Son Indicted for Employment Tax and Wire Fraud Schemes
body: Press Release Staffing Business Owner and Son Indicted for Employment Tax and Wire Fraud Schemes Thursday, October 15, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release Office of Public Affairs Created False Workers’ Compensation Insurance Policy Certificates to Deceive Clients A federal grand jury in the District of Minnesota returned an indictment today charging Ku Kelvin Vue and his son, Travis Vue, with willfully failing to collect, account for and pay over employment taxes to the IRS on behalf of the staffing business they operated, and conspiracy to commit wire fraud. Ku Kelvin Vue was also charged with willfully failing to file corporate tax returns, and Travis Vue was charged with filing a false individual tax return and willfully failing to file individual tax returns. The following is according to the indictment: Ku Kelvin Vue was the owner and president of UniSelect Services Inc., a temporary staffing agency that provided temporary workers to client companies in the manufacturing industry and other industries. Travis Vue helped run the company as early as 2014. Both men were allegedly responsible for withholding Social Security, Medicare and income taxes from UniSelect’s employees’ wages and paying those withholdings over to the IRS, as well as filing quarterly tax returns with the IRS documenting those withholdings. According to the indictment, however, from the third quarter of 2020 through the second quarter of 2022, neither Ku Kelvin Vue nor Travis Vue collected those taxes or paid them over to the IRS, nor filed quarterly tax returns with the IRS. The indictment also alleges that Ku Kelvin Vue willfully failed to file corporate tax returns on behalf of UniSelect for the years 2020 through 2022. It is alleged that Travis Vue willfully failed to file individual tax returns for the years 2021 through 2023. Travis Vue also allegedly filed a false tax return for 2020 reporting zero wages or income, even though he received substantially greater wages and income during that year and was required to file a tax return. In addition to their tax crimes, the indictment also charges Ku Kelvin Vue and Travis Vue with one count each of conspiracy to commit wire fraud. According to the indictment, the Vues conspired to secure business for UniSelect by falsely assuring clients the company maintained active workers’ compensation insurance coverage for all UniSelect employees furnished to the clients as temporary workers. In reality, UniSelect allegedly did not maintain workers’ compensation insurance coverage on behalf of its workers. Instead, Kelvin Vue and Travis Vue allegedly conspired to create false and fraudulent workers’ compensation insurance policy certificates, which they provided to clients to deceive them into believing UniSelect maintained insurance coverage. Both defendants face maximum penalties of 20 years in prison for the wire fraud conspiracy count, five years in prison for each count of willful failure to collect, account for and pay over employment taxes and one year in prison for each count of willful failure to file a tax return. Travis Vue also faces a maximum penalty of three years in prison for filing a false tax return. Assistant Attorney General Colin M. McDonald of the Justice Department’s National Fraud Enforcement Division and U.S. Attorney Daniel Rosen for the District of Minnesota made the announcement. IRS Criminal Investigation is investigating the case. Assistant Deputy Chief Eric B. Powers and Trial Attorney Megan E. Wessel of the Fraud Division’s Tax Section are prosecuting the case. On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the Fraud Division. The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs. An indictment is merely an allegation. All defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law. Updated October 15, 2026 Topic Fraud Component National Fraud Enforcement Division Press Release Number: 26-1213

Ku Kelvin Vue was also charged with willfully failing to file corporate tax returns, and Travis Vue was charged with filing a false individual tax return and willfully failing to file individual tax returns.

title: Founder And Former Ceo Of 777 Partners Pleads Guilty To $500 Million Fraud Scheme
body: Press Release Founder And Former Ceo Of 777 Partners Pleads Guilty To $500 Million Fraud Scheme Thursday, October 15, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Southern District of New York Joshua Wander Pleads Guilty to Wire Fraud and Securities Fraud in Connection With Scheme to Defraud 777 Partners’ Lenders and Investors United States Attorney for the Southern District of New York, Jamie McDonald, announced today that JOSHUA WANDER, the founder and former CEO of 777 Partners, a Miami-based investment firm, pled guilty to wire fraud and securities fraud in connection with a scheme to defraud the lenders and investors of 777 Partners.  As part of his plea, WANDER agreed to forfeit at least $500,000,000 in proceeds from his illegal scheme.  WANDER pled guilty today before U.S. District Judge J. Paul Oetken. “This Office, together with our law enforcement partners, will continue to protect investors and lenders and to ensure that those who threaten our financial markets are held accountable,” said U.S Attorney Jamie McDonald. “As he has now admitted, Josh Wander used his company, 777 Partners, to steal hundreds of millions of dollars from private creditors and investors. Wander double-pledged assets, pledged fictitious assets, lied about the financial condition of his company, and even falsified bank statements, all to gain access to his victims’ funds.  He then put those funds to uses that his lenders never permitted, including footing the bill for 777’s collection of professional soccer teams.  Whether perpetrated in the private or public markets, such brazen conduct undermines the integrity of our financial system and will not be tolerated.” As alleged in the Indictment and other public filings in this case: WANDER, the co-founder and former CEO of 777 Partners, a private investment firm, orchestrated a multi-year scheme to defraud 777 Partners’ lenders and investors of more than $500,000,000. 777 Partners’ initial and primary business model was to underwrite and finance structured settlements. Over time, WANDER began investing capital in new sectors, including airlines and professional sports teams. 777 Partners lacked the funds to pay for these new acquisitions, and WANDER directed that restricted funds from 777 Partners’ lenders in its structured settlement business be used to cover the firm’s acquisitions and expenses. To steal these funds from lenders, WANDER pledged to his lenders hundreds of millions of dollars of structured settlement assets that 777 Partners had never purchased or had previously pledged to other lenders. To conceal the fraud, WANDER directed employees to digitally alter bank account statements to reflects millions of dollars in cash on hand that the firm did not have. In 2021 and 2022, WANDER raised more than $200 million in outside investments in 777 Partners through the sale of preferred equity interests in 777 Partners and an affiliated entity. WANDER misrepresented the financial condition of the firm in soliciting these investments. In addition, in March 2022, WANDER solicited a $20 million loan from a lender. WANDER provided the lender with dozens of doctored bank account statements to conceal that WANDER had misappropriated the funds, spending millions of dollars of options trades. By March 2023, WANDER’s scheme began to unravel. One of the firm’s lenders confronted WANDER about allegations of double-pledged assets, and WANDER falsely claimed there had been an error caused by 777 Partners’ antiquated computer system. A few days later, WANDER again falsely assured the lender, among other things, that the double-pledging had been inadvertent. In 2024, WANDER resigned as CEO. *                *                * WANDER, 45, of Florida, pled guilty to one count of wire fraud and securities fraud, each of which carries a maximum sentence of 20 years in prison. The maximum potential sentence in this case is prescribed by Congress and provided here for informational purposes only, as any sentencing of the defendant will be determined by the judge. WANDER is scheduled to be sentenced by U.S. District Judge Oetken on March 1, 2027. Mr. McDonald praised the outstanding work of the Federal Bureau of Investigation and Homeland Security Investigations. Mr. McDonald also expressed appreciation for the assistance of the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission. This case is being handled by the Office’s Securities and Commodities Fraud Task Force. Assistant U.S. Attorneys Thomas S. Burnett, Marguerite B. Colson, Sarah Mortazavi, and Alexandra N. Rothman are in charge of the prosecution. Contact Nicholas Biase, Shelby Wratchford (212) 637-2600 Updated October 15, 2026 Topic Financial Fraud Component USAO - New York, Southern Press Release Number: 26-294

title: United States Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of Alabama Joins DOJ Fraud Division, IRS, and IRS-CI in National Tax Enforcement Surge Exposing over $490 Million in Tax Fraud
body: Press Release United States Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of Alabama Joins DOJ Fraud Division, IRS, and IRS-CI in National Tax Enforcement Surge Exposing over $490 Million in Tax Fraud Thursday, October 15, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Southern District of Alabama MOBILE, AL – The United States Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of Alabama today announced sentencings as part of a nationwide enforcement actions led by the Justice Department’s National Fraud Enforcement Division, Internal Revenue Service, and Internal Revenue Service Criminal Investigation (IRS-CI) targeting tax fraud and related offenses. The United States Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of Alabama was key participant in this surge effort.  Several defendants were sentenced for defrauding the United States of millions of dollars intended for businesses impacted by the COVID-19 pandemic. Between early September and today, federal prosecutors across the country facilitated fraud enforcement actions spanning over 76 criminal defendants, whose alleged crimes resulted in over $490,000,000 in intended loss to American taxpayers. Earlier this month, Echandza Maxie (Echandza), 43, and her husband, Glennie McGee (McGee), 42, both of Mobile, were sentenced to 20 years in federal prison for their roles in a scheme to defraud the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) by illegally obtaining more than $1.5 million in COVID-19-related tax credits intended to provide relief to legitimate businesses and individuals during the pandemic. Three additional defendants were convicted and sentenced for their roles in a related scheme to defraud the Small Business Administration (SBA) through fraudulent applications for COVID-19 relief loans. A sixth defendant was separately sentenced for his role in the tax fraud scheme.  In total, the defendants were ordered to pay over $2.4 Million in restitution to the IRS and SBA for their crimes. In response to the COVID-19 pandemic and its economic impact, Congress authorized refundable tax credits for paid sick and family leave to reimburse eligible employers and self-employed individuals for qualifying leave related to COVID-19. Congress also established the Paycheck Protection Program (PPP) and Economic Injury Disaster Loan (EIDL) program to provide emergency financial assistance to legitimate businesses suffering economic losses during the pandemic. During a cocaine-trafficking investigation involving a court-authorized wiretap of a telephone belonging to John David Clarke of Mobile, Alabama, the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), working with IRS-CI, uncovered a large-scale tax fraud scheme. Federal agents determined that Echandza, her husband, McGee, Echandza’s sister, Edeszann Maxie (Edeszann), Tiveria Populus (Populus), Jamael Nettles (Nettles), John David Clarke (Clarke), and others participated in schemes to fraudulently obtain COVID-19-related tax credits and SBA loans. According to court documents, Echandza owned and operated a Mobile tax-preparation business known as “Self Made Taxes,” which was purportedly co-located with a clothing store, an eyelash business, and other businesses. Edeszann, who also worked as a tax preparer, worked with Echandza, McGee, and others to obtain the personal identifying information of prospective taxpayers and use that information to file fraudulent tax returns in their names. The defendants enlisted recruiters who were paid finder’s fees to obtain names, dates of birth, and Social Security numbers belonging to prospective taxpayers. Echandza, Edeszann, and McGee generally required only that the prospective taxpayer had not yet filed a tax return and did not owe child support. They did not obtain information necessary to determine whether the taxpayer actually operated a business or otherwise qualified for the COVID-19 tax credits. Using the personal identifying information they obtained, Echandza and Edeszann fabricated fictitious self-employed businesses, frequently claiming that the taxpayers operated landscaping or hairstyling businesses. The fraudulent tax returns routinely claimed that the taxpayers had taken the maximum amount of COVID-19-related sick and family leave and sought the maximum available credit of approximately $30,000 per return. Echandza and Edeszann also fabricated business revenues for the 2021 tax year. Many of the fraudulent refunds were directed to bank accounts controlled by the defendants. Although the IRS identified and rejected a significant number of fraudulent returns after placing identity-theft holds on them, the scheme nevertheless generated more than $1.5 million in fraudulent tax refunds. Some individuals whose information was used in the scheme believed they were legitimately eligible to receive COVID-19 relief and trusted the defendants to prepare accurate tax returns on their behalf. Some individuals unfamiliar with the tax-filing process paid between $10,000 and $15,000 to have their returns prepared, believing the payments were legitimate tax-preparation fees. FBI and IRS-CI special agents identified dozens of individuals whose personal information had been used to file fraudulent tax returns. Many had no knowledge that a return had been filed in their names. Others were unaware that their returns contained false information, including claims that they operated businesses they did not own or operate. In some instances, the defendants filed fraudulent returns as “self-prepared,” even though the returns had been prepared and submitted by Echandza or Edeszann. Investigators identified the fraud through contact and banking information on the returns that belonged to the defendants, demonstrating that the named taxpayers had no knowledge of the refunds generated using their personal information. In other cases, individuals learned that fraudulent returns had been filed in their names after receiving notice from the Social Security Administration that their disability benefits could be affected by purported business income reported to the IRS. Fraudulent SBA Loans The defendants, except for Nettles, also fraudulently applied for and obtained dozens of PPP and EIDL loans administered by the SBA in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. The PPP provided eligible businesses with potentially forgivable loans guaranteed by the SBA, while the EIDL program provided low-interest loans to help eligible small businesses maintain operations during the pandemic. The programs were intended to provide financial assistance for legitimate business expenses, including payroll, rent, and utilities. With assistance from special agents with the SBA Office of Inspector General, investigators determined that Echandza, McGee, Edeszann, Clarke, and Populus each submitted fraudulent SBA loan applications. The applications contained material misrepresentations that the defendants operated legitimate businesses before the pandemic and that those businesses generated substantial revenue. For businesses that had some evidence of operation before 2020, investigators determined that the defendants fabricated revenue figures and the number of employees to obtain larger loan proceeds. In total, the defendants obtained more than $885,000 in SBA loans to which they were not entitled. Each defendant pleaded guilty to charges arising from his or her participation in the fraud schemes. United States District Court Judge Terry F. Moorer imposed the sentences. Sentences Echandza Maxie was sentenced to 20 years in prison, followed by a mandatory two-year consecutive sentence for aggravated identity theft. She was ordered to pay $1,576,358.88 in restitution to the IRS and $257,413.93 to the SBA. Her 20-year sentence, excluding the mandatory consecutive sentence for aggravated identity theft, was ordered to run concurrently with her life sentence stemming from a multi-million-dollar cocaine and fentanyl trafficking organization related convictions. If released from prison, she will be subject to three years of supervised release. She was also ordered to pay a $300 special assessment and forfeit approximately $85,000 in fraud proceeds seized by the FBI during the investigation. Glennie McGee was sentenced to 20 years in prison, followed by a mandatory two-year consecutive sentence for aggravated identity theft. McGee was ordered to pay $672,219 in restitution to the IRS and $340,910.16 to the SBA. His 20-year sentence, excluding the mandatory consecutive sentence for aggravated identity theft, was ordered to run concurrently with his life sentence stemming from his multi-million-dollar cocaine and fentanyl trafficking organization. If released from prison, he will be subject to three years of supervised release. He was also ordered to pay a $300 special assessment. Edeszann Maxie was sentenced to 135 months in prison, followed by a mandatory two-year consecutive sentence for aggravated identity theft. She was ordered to pay $187,301 in restitution to the IRS and $298,667.70 to the SBA. Upon release from prison, she will be subject to three years of supervised release. She was also ordered to pay a $300 special assessment. John David Clarke was sentenced to 20 years in prison and ordered to pay $28,764.10 in restitution to the IRS and $55,167 to the SBA. His sentence was ordered to run concurrently with his separately imposed 20-year-sentence stemming from his convictions related to a large-scale cocaine trafficking conspiracy . Upon release from prison, Clarke will be subject to three years of supervised release. He was also ordered to pay a $200 special assessment. Tiveria Populus was sentenced to time served and ordered to pay $28,764.10 in restitution to the IRS and $46,206.29 to the SBA. Populus will be subject to five years of supervised release and was ordered to pay a $200 special assessment. Jamael Nettles, in a separate case, was sentenced to five days in prison and ordered to pay $29,339 in restitution to the IRS. Nettles will be subject to three years of supervised release and was ordered to pay a $100 special assessment. “The defendants exploited programs created to provide relief to businesses and individuals during an unprecedented national crisis, stealing millions of dollars through fraudulent tax returns and applications for pandemic relief,” said U.S. Attorney Sean P. Costello. “Fraud of this kind does more than steal money from the government—it undermines the integrity of our tax system and diverts resources away from the people and businesses who were entitled to receive them. I commend IRS Criminal Investigation and our other law enforcement partners for following the financial trail, uncovering this scheme, and holding fraudsters responsible.” “The defendants carried out a coordinated scheme to defraud the government by filing fraudulent tax returns, misusing personal identities, and submitting false pandemic relief loan applications,” said Special Agent in Charge Demetrius Hardeman, IRS Criminal Investigation, Atlanta Field Office. “IRS Criminal Investigation special agents, working closely with our federal partners, traced the movement of illicit proceeds and uncovered the financial trails that revealed the full extent of the conspiracy. Their efforts ensured that those responsible were identified and held accountable.” The case was investigated by the Federal Bureau of Investigation, IRS Criminal Investigation, the Department of Homeland Security, Homeland Security Investigations, the Small Business Administration Office of Inspector General, and the Social Security Administration, with assistance from multiple state and local law enforcement agencies, including the Mobile County Sheriff’s Office and Mobile Police Department. Assistant U.S. Attorneys Kasee S. Heisterhagen and Justin Kopf prosecuted the case on behalf of the United States. In addition to its outstanding financial impact, this prosecution was also a part of the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) initiative established by Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion. The HSTF is a whole-of-government partnership focused on investigating and prosecuting criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and trafficking organizations operating in the United States and abroad. Through interagency collaboration, the HSTF directs federal law enforcement resources toward investigating and prosecuting crimes committed by these organizations. HSTF Mobile includes agents and officers from, among others, Homeland Security Investigations, the Federal Bureau of Investigation, the Drug Enforcement Administration, and the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives, with prosecutions led by the United States Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of Alabama. On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the National Fraud Enforcement Division (Fraud Division). The Fraud Division investigates and prosecutes individuals and organizations that commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s efforts to combat fraud support President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to address fraud, waste, and abuse involving federal benefit programs. This press release details one way in which this office has contributed to ensuring that all Americans pay their fair share. To see the successes of other offices, please see this press release . If you believe you are a victim of identity theft or suspect a paid tax return preparer is engaged in fraud or misconduct, you may report it to the IRS and make a complaint about a tax return preparer online . Individuals with information about allegations of fraud involving COVID-19 are encouraged to report it by calling the Department of Justice’s National Center for Disaster Fraud (NCDF) Hotline at 866-720-5721 or via the NCDF Web Complaint Form at: https://www.justice.gov/disaster-fraud/ncdf-disaster-complaint-form . title: South L.A. Man Arraigned on Federal Charges that He Sex Trafficked Minors on Figueroa Corridor and Attempted to Kidnap Woman at Phone Store
body: Press Release South L.A. Man Arraigned on Federal Charges that He Sex Trafficked Minors on Figueroa Corridor and Attempted to Kidnap Woman at Phone Store Thursday, October 15, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Central District of California LOS ANGELES – A South Los Angeles man was arraigned today on a four-count federal indictment charging him with violently sex trafficking two teenage girls on the Figueroa Corridor, plying at least one of them with narcotics, and with attempting to kidnap a woman at a mobile phone store after she escaped his apartment while he was physically attacking her. Derrick Harrison Enrico Brooks, Jr., 31, of Baldwin Village, is charged with two counts of sex trafficking of children by force, fraud, or coercion, one count of distribution of controlled substances to a person under 21, and one count of attempted kidnapping. Brooks pleaded not guilty to all charges at his arraignment today in United States District Court in downtown Los Angeles. His trial is scheduled for December 1. Last month a federal magistrate judge ordered him detained without bond. According to the complaint, indictment, and other court documents, in November 2025, Brooks sex trafficked a 15-year-old girl – identified in court documents as “Minor Victim 1.” Brooks and this victim traveled from California to Colorado in his green limousine for commercial sex work. Brooks demanded that she earn $1,000 per day, physically assaulted her several times, and at one point, caused the victim to think she was going to die from his physical violence. Brooks posted an advertisement of her on the Craigslist website. Minor Victim 1 returned to Los Angeles and escaped from Brooks while working on the Figueroa Corridor, a 3.5-mile stretch of Figueroa Street in South Los Angeles that is notorious for prostitution activity. In January and February of 2026, Brooks trafficked a 17-year-old girl, identified in court documents as “Minor Victim 2,” who also worked on the Figueroa Corridor. Brooks physically assaulted this victim as well and knowingly distributed Ecstasy to her. In August 2026, Brooks assaulted and attempted to kidnap a woman – identified in the indictment as “Victim 3” – in a mobile phone store in Baldwin Village. Victim 3 had fled Brooks’s nearby apartment after he choked her and punched her in the face. Two weeks after the attempted kidnapping, law enforcement arrested Brooks in connection with that incident. An indictment merely contains allegations. All defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law. If convicted of all charges, Brooks would face a mandatory minimum sentence of 15 years in federal prison and a statutory maximum sentence of life imprisonment. The FBI is investigating this matter with assistance from the Los Angeles Police Department, Pomona Police Department, and the Los Angeles County District Attorney’s Office. Assistant United States Attorneys Chelsea Norell and Mirelle Raza of the Major Crimes Section are prosecuting this case. Contact Ciaran McEvoy Public Information Officer ciaran.mcevoy@usdoj.gov (213) 894-4465 Updated October 15, 2026 Topic Violent Crime Component USAO - California, Central Press Release Number: 26-197

title: NVIDIA Expands Advanced Technology Access for Europe’s Scientific Community Through Open Learning Resources, Collaborations and Compute
body: NVIDIA Expands Advanced Technology Access for Europe’s Scientific Community Through Open Learning Resources, Collaborations and Compute NVIDIA’s participation in the European Commission’s AI in Science Enablers Initiative deepens its commitment to supporting the pursuit of scientific progress across the region. October 15, 2026 by Rod Evans 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Much of today’s scientific progress begins with computation. But turning accelerated computing’s potential into scientific progress — modeling climate systems, designing molecules, simulating materials and more — depends on more than breakthrough technology. Especially for smaller labs, early-career scientists or science-based startups, the hardest part of research can be everything that comes before the science: assembling tools, finding compute and building the expertise to use both. At the AI in Science Summit in Dublin today, the European Commission launched the AI in Science Enablers Initiative, a shared framework connected to RAISE — the Resource for AI Science in Europe — that brings private-sector support closer to Europe’s research community. Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements NVIDIA is joining the campaign , providing: Access to accelerated tools, models and platforms Compute, cloud resources, data and scientific resources Skills, training and technical support Collaborative projects and pilots along with support for researchers and talent Support for startups and ecosystem development “Europe’s ambition in AI in science can only become reality if we bring together the strengths of our research community, industry and other partners,” Ekaterina Zaharieva, European Commissioner for Startups, Research and Innovation. “Through the AI in Science Enablers campaign, we are turning this ambition into concrete commitments that give researchers access to the tools, expertise and resources they need to innovate.” Open Models NVIDIA’s pledge begins with open source technology. NVIDIA has released more than 250 open models, 250 open datasets and over 1,400 open source software projects spanning large language models, healthcare, robotics, climate science, physical AI, autonomous vehicles and scientific research. The models and datasets are available on Hugging Face and GitHub. Building on this open ecosystem, researchers can build agentic reasoning capabilities with NVIDIA Nemotron — a family of architectures, open weights, open source models, training data and recipes — and scientific software including NVIDIA BioNeMo Agent Toolkit , NVIDIA PhysicsNeMo libraries, NVIDIA Earth-2 models and NVIDIA ALCHEMI NIM microservices to accelerate research across biology, chemistry, molecular design, weather and climate, energy, engineering, physics and material sciences. Skills and Training Building advanced intelligence capability across Europe requires knowledge that travels as freely as compute. The NVIDIA Deep Learning Institute has launched a new open source courseware hub with hands-on course materials covering accelerated computing and deep learning — freely downloadable and openly licensed, with no enrollment, fees or deadline. Modular by design, the courses can be adapted for university curricula, supercomputing center bootcamps or developer community events, and serve as a direct bridge to NVIDIA’s broader training and certification programs . Access to Compute NVIDIA is collaborating with cloud infrastructure partners and European national AI factories — including in France , Spain and Sweden — to open new routes for startups and small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) to access sovereign European compute and services. The NVIDIA Inception program for startups provides access to compute resources and technical support, lowering the barrier to entry for startups seeking high-performance infrastructure and technological education. AI2F in France is the first AI factory to have collaborated with the Inception program for four months, demonstrating strong results. The BSC AI Factory ran a pilot initiative and is now rolling out its first full accelerator program, with growing interest from other European national AI factories in replicating the model in 2027. Beyond startup support, this program is designed to contribute to a broader strategic objective: building self-sustaining AI ventures in Spain and Europe. Sweden AI Factory , one of Europe’s 19 EuroHPC-funded AI factories, announced a collaboration with NVIDIA to open its infrastructure and expertise to Inception startups and SMEs enterprises across sectors including life and material sciences, autonomous systems and gaming. Finally, EuroHPC supercomputing centers such as CINECA and JSC provide academia and startups with free access to NVIDIA GPU infrastructure and services for open research. NVIDIA complements this access with office hours, bootcamps and hackathons that help researchers fine-tune models on their own datasets. As an example, NVIDIA is co-organizing an European AI hackathon this month alongside Austrian Scientific Computing , the Leibniz Supercomputing Centre , the High-Performance Computing Center Stuttgart and The Cyprus Institute, for Pharos-CY . AI Infrastructure Expansion To top it all off, NVIDIA is powering Europe’s most ambitious expansion of AI infrastructure to date, with 35 supercomputers currently in development across the continent — the largest single-year buildout of supercomputing capacity Europe has ever seen. Together, these systems will equip over 3 million researchers with next-generation infrastructure, accelerating discovery across domains from climate science and drug development to materials research and beyond. Explore NVIDIA technologies for science and open source courseware , and find hands-on training through the NVIDIA Deep Learning Institute . Follow the European Commission’s RAISE Pledging Initiative . title: The Nordics and NVIDIA Show What’s Possible When a Region Commits to Advanced Computing
body: The Nordics and NVIDIA Show What’s Possible When a Region Commits to Advanced Computing From building sovereign infrastructure and autonomous trucks to quantum-GPU supercomputing, Nordic countries are embracing and accelerating technological development. October 14, 2026 by Linda Malm 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! The Nordic countries have become the European leader in unicorn startup density, producing the most emerging companies valued at $1 billion or more per capita on the continent. Now, a new chapter for the region is unfolding as countries race to build one of Europe’s most consequential technology ecosystems. The many computing advancements already underway in the Nordics, combined with the opportunity that lies ahead, signal a region moving from ambition to application. NVIDIA’s Investments in the Nordics Over the past year, NVIDIA has invested in the technology ecosystem in the Nordics, including Sweden’s leading startups Lovable and Legora. Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements Lovable , a Stockholm-based startup, provides a software creation platform that enables anyone to build and run software using plain language. In collaboration with NVIDIA, Lovable is optimizing inference for open models and training its models using NVIDIA Dynamo software and Nemotron tools. Legora provides an agentic operating system for legal work, supporting lawyers in research, review and drafting across complex matters. Nordics Emerge as Infrastructure Hub The foundation for establishing the Nordics as a technology powerhouse is already being built and the region holds a structural advantage: abundant renewable energy, rigorous data governance and a research tradition that bridges academia and industry. The Nordics are one of Europe’s fastest growing hubs for infrastructure. AI clouds are expanding with a projected 1 gigawatts of capacity to be deployed across the region by the end of 2027. Among these cloud providers are Bitdeer, CoreWeave , Crusoe , Hyperstack, Nscale , Verda and Volta . In Sweden, a consortium anchored by Ericsson, AstraZeneca, Saab, SEB and Wallenberg Investments, with SKF as strategic partner, launched Sferical One — a shared supercomputer running on two NVIDIA DGX SuperPODs with 16 racks of NVIDIA DGX GB300 systems and 1,152 GPUs. The consortium will build services using NVIDIA Nemotron open models, which allow researchers to customize and deploy their models in a secure environment. Nordic-Built Intelligence Some of the Nordics’ leading technology companies are now building proprietary intelligence on NVIDIA infrastructure. Spotify , which personalizes music, podcasts and audiobooks for hundreds of millions of listeners, uses NVIDIA TensorRT-LLM inference software to run AI-powered podcast recommendations faster and cheaper at scale. The deployment is a case study in inference efficiency: delivering the same recommendations to a global audience at a lower cost per query. ABB Robotics developed RobotStudio HyperReality using NVIDIA Omniverse libraries to bridge the gap between robot simulations and real-world performance. By combining NVIDIA’s advanced simulation capabilities with ABB Robotics’ virtual controller, running the same firmware as its physical robots, the solution enables engineers to train, test and validate robots virtually, while using real-world data to continuously improve the digital model. According to ABB Robotics, the solution delivers up to 99% simulation accuracy and reduces commissioning time by up to 80%. Finnish telecom company Elisa is launching a beta of Moontalk AIRI, a real-time enterprise agentic assistant that retrieves information, captures insights and documents decisions during meetings and calls. Built on NVIDIA Nemotron open models and distributed infrastructure, it uses company data and low-latency networking to deliver fast, context-aware responses. Nordic Startups Scaling on NVIDIA Sweden’s startup ecosystem raised $2.8 billion in the first half of 2026 and is projected to reach $5 billion for the year. This next generation is building fast — and on open models. Stilta is reinventing how companies protect their inventions with intellectual property. The Stockholm-based startup is post-training NVIDIA Nemotron open models to scale patent analysis from a single patent to entire portfolios — work that was previously out of reach. Nemotron gives Stilta the language model accuracy for continuous portfolio monitoring at scale, across the thousands of patents that large industrial and technology companies hold. ConfidentialMind’s SampoTron , built on NVIDIA Nemotron-3-Embed, delivers more than 20% improvement in cross-lingual retrieval accuracy across English, Finnish and Swedish. Agaton , a platform that analyzes customer conversations in real time, is using NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning to speed up Revenue Mining solution on live sales calls. By routing knowledge retrieval to Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, Agaton can cut response latency to deliver fast responses that inform customers’ buying decisions. Klang , a Swedish speech lab, fine-tuned the NVIDIA Parakeet v3 model to create Pianissimo — a Swedish transcription model that reduces errors by 75% while being 64x faster than the most accurate alternative. Built on over 50,000 hours of Swedish speech using the open source NVIDIA NeMo framework, the model is freely available on Hugging Face. Embedl , founded in Gothenburg and a member of the NVIDIA Inception program for cutting-edge startups, and Space Cargo Unlimited unveiled an onboard prototype that monitors protein crystallization, flags anomalies and recommends actions on a single NVIDIA Jetson Orin NX module, without continuous ground connectivity. Sweden AI Factory — one of Europe’s 19 EuroHPC-funded AI factories — announced a collaboration with NVIDIA to open its infrastructure and expertise to Inception startups and small- and medium-sized enterprises across industries, including life and material sciences, autonomous systems and gaming. Autonomous Machines on Nordic Roads and Factory Floors In Sweden, advanced computing is also powering vehicles on the road and machines in factories. Volvo Cars is combining its industry-leading vehicle safety systems and engineering expertise with NVIDIA Hyperion , Halos OS and Alpamayo Stack to enable future Volvo cars to safely navigate complex real-world environments from door to door. Autonomous freight company Einride is building its next-generation Einride Driver on NVIDIA Hyperion for autonomous freight trucks, using the NVIDIA Halos safety system and NVIDIA Cosmos open world models. Meanwhile, Toyota Material Handling Europe — the world’s leading forklift manufacturer — is bringing autonomous machines to factory floors. In a collaboration with NVIDIA and SoftServe, Toyota Material Handling Europe is adopting a simulation-first approach to autonomous material handling, cutting autonomous solution deployment time by up to 50% across its global engineering, manufacturing and innovation teams. Norrsken Foundation and NVIDIA are opening the Stockholm AI Lab, a physical hub for AI-native founders working on global challenges, set to open in 2027. Quantum Meets Accelerated Computing Finally, Swedish companies are advancing quantum research using NVIDIA’s quantum computing platform. Stockholm-based FirstQFM used NVIDIA accelerated computing to train a model that reduces the execution time of quantum processors by 33% without sacrificing performance. Validated on a QuantWare quantum processor unit, this model optimizes how the operations needed by quantum algorithms are turned into detailed hardware instructions, accounting for detailed updates on how the hardware is calibrated. Tune in to NVIDIA founder and CEO Jensen Huang’s GTC Berlin keynote on Wednesday, Oct. 21, at 11 a.m. CEST.
